Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test "testClassInstantiationWithParameterBeingNullThrowsNullPointerExceptionTwo" expects a NullPointerException to be thrown when constructing a ChecksumCalculatingInputStream with a null Checksum parameter. The constructor code snippet reveals that it simply assigns the provided checksum and input stream parameters to internal fields without any null check or validation. Hence, the constructor itself does not throw a NullPointerException even if checksum is null.

The current bug report suggests that a NullPointerException occurs in the getValue() method of ChecksumCalculatingInputStream. Inspecting getValue(), it directly calls checksum.getValue(). If checksum is null (as allowed by the constructor currently), calling getValue() on a null reference results in a NullPointerException.

Thus, the root cause is that the constructor of ChecksumCalculatingInputStream does not validate against null for its checksum parameter. Subsequent calls to getValue() on such improperly constructed objects cause NullPointerExceptions. The test expecting an exception at construction fails because no exception is raised there.

No recent bug reports directly relate to construction null checks or getValue method issues in ChecksumCalculatingInputStream, so they are not particularly relevant for this diagnosis.

To fix this defect, the constructor of ChecksumCalculatingInputStream should be modified to throw NullPointerException if checksum is null, ensuring fail-fast behavior that aligns with the test expectation and prevents downstream errors.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
